summary.headline: Sagar Cements Q1 FY27: volumes up ~13% YoY but loss after tax of ₹28 crore and EBITDA of ₹451/tonne on West Asia-driven cost inflation.
summary.overview: Volumes grew about 13% YoY and revenue rose 5% YoY, with realisations broadly stable. Profitability moderated as energy, fuel and packaging costs rose amid West Asia tensions, leaving EBITDA at ₹451 per tonne and a loss after tax of ₹28 crore. Management maintained a 7 million tonne volume target for FY27 (excluding clinker) and reiterated FY27 EBITDA guidance of ₹500–550 per tonne, down from the earlier ~₹600 reference raised by an analyst. Capex completed in the quarter includes Jeerabad 0.5 million tonne expansion and the remaining 1.55 MW of Gudipadu waste heat recovery; the 0.75 million tonne Andhra Cements expansion is expected by quarter-end.

segments.name: Mattampally (Telangana)
segments.commentary: Utilisation 65% in Q1; debt-free per management and carries waste heat recovery, which keeps its grid power cost lower.

segments.name: Gudipadu (AP)
segments.commentary: Utilisation 79% in Q1; remaining 1.55 MW of the 4.35 MW waste heat recovery commissioned, with ~₹25/tonne consolidated saving expected.

segments.name: Jeerabad (MP)
segments.commentary: Utilisation 96% in Q1; 0.5 million tonne expansion completed, with ramp-up expected as soon as possible and some clinker still sold until volumes stabilise.

segments.name: Andhra Cements
segments.commentary: Utilisation near 50%, targeted at ~60% by end-FY27 and 60–70% thereafter; variable cost ~₹100–125/tonne above Mattampally due to grid power with no waste heat recovery; new cement mill due end-September.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume target of ~7 million tonnes, excluding clinker sales; management sees FY28 volume growth in double digits.
FY27 EBITDA guidance of ₹500–550 per tonne, assuming prices stay flat; management said ₹550 is 'definitely doable'.
Q2 FY27 to see cost increase from maintenance shutdowns at three plants (Mattampally, Jeerabad among them) and inventory cost adjustment; management expects recovery in Q3 and Q4.
Management pencilled in ~₹100/tonne cost inflation (₹50 power and fuel, ₹50 miscellaneous), offset by efficiency gains; inventory covers operations up to mid-October.
No capex plans beyond ~₹30–40 crore annual maintenance through 2028, apart from ~₹240 crore of ongoing capex spread over FY27 and FY28.
Vizag land monetisation of ₹150 crore pencilled for FY27 and ~₹200 crore for FY28, pending a generic Government GO.
capex_capacity: Jeerabad 0.5 million tonne capacity expansion completed in Q1; Madhya Pradesh volumes expected to rise after this.
Gudipadu 1.55 MW waste heat recovery commissioned, completing 4.35 MW total installed capacity.
Andhra Cements 0.75 million tonne cement capacity expansion expected to complete before end of Q2 FY27.
New cement mill at Andhra due for commissioning end-September 2026.
Andhra waste heat recovery planned in the next couple of years, expected to deliver savings similar to Gudipadu's.
Super fine building material work has started; operational plan to be shared by end of Q2.
demand_pricing: South footprint ~80% of volumes; AP and Telangana combined Q1 demand up ~11% YoY, Tamil Nadu ~4% (April negative, June ~20%), Kerala ~12%, Karnataka flat; South demand ~6–6.5% YTD, expected at 8–10% for FY27.
Madhya Pradesh demand grew ~9–10%; Maharashtra and Odisha described as healthy.
July demand expected to track Q1 trend, with labour availability back.
Prices rose early in Q1 but moderated late in the quarter; flat from March exit to July, with a ₹50–60/tonne realisation gain cited.
Management expects price hikes eventually, citing flat cement inflation over 10 years against substantial cost inflation; timing and size uncertain amid competitive intensity.
Tamil Nadu ban on transport of rough stones and aggregates to other states: management sees no impact.
Heat waves and election-related labour shortages in Eastern and Southern India disrupted Q1 execution.
